description: Machine-readable candidate field/concept crosswalks. These mappings are non-normative and do not claim standards conformance, certification, or authenticated identity unless separately evidenced.

profiles.source_version: OTLP current; GenAI conventions development snapshot 2026-09-18
profiles.notes: Telemetry is observed execution evidence. Authorization, materiality, and principal identity remain separate evidence.

mappings.transform: Validate 32 hexadecimal characters, reject all-zero value, normalize lowercase.
mappings.notes: One logical GenAI trace is adapted per candidate record.

mappings.transform: Validate 16 hexadecimal characters, reject all-zero value, normalize lowercase, prefix with 'otel-span:'.
mappings.notes: Provides stable event identity within the adapted trace.

mappings.transform: Convert Unix nanoseconds to RFC 3339 UTC while preserving significant nanosecond digits.
mappings.notes: This preserves source timestamp precision but does not prove source clock accuracy.

mappings.transform: Require one unambiguous value across the adapted trace unless explicitly overridden by sidecar context.
mappings.notes: OpenTelemetry describes the instrumented agent identity; deployments still need separate authentication/trust policy for security identity.

mappings.transform: Use gen_ai.agent.version when uniquely available; otherwise allow service.version or explicit sidecar override.
mappings.notes: Version metadata is descriptive evidence.
Provider semantic-convention value is preserved when present and unambiguous.
Request model metadata is preserved when present and unambiguous.

mappings.transform: For execute_tool spans use gen_ai.tool.name; otherwise preserve gen_ai.operation.name.
mappings.notes: This yields an operation value that can be compared with delegated authority scope.

mappings.source_expression: OTLP span status, endTimeUnixNano, and error.type
mappings.transform: Error -> failed; missing end time -> pending; otherwise completed, unless stronger sidecar evidence supplies an override.
mappings.notes: Execution status is not authorization status.
Materiality and source role are supplied separately; presence in telemetry does not make a source material.
Tool arguments may contain sensitive content and are intentionally not copied into the canonical record.
Tool results may contain sensitive content and are intentionally not copied into the canonical record.

profiles.notes: MCP protocol metadata is observed/descriptive evidence. Authenticated identity and authorization come from a separate control-plane sidecar in the current adapter.

mappings.notes: The adapter also requires the response id to match.
Mcp-Name is checked against params.name when the routing header is present.
This timestamp belongs to the capture substrate, not to the MCP wire schema itself.

mappings.source_expression: JSON-RPC error or tools/call result state
mappings.transform: JSON-RPC error or isError -> failed; input_required -> pending; otherwise completed, unless stronger sidecar evidence overrides.
mappings.notes: Successful protocol execution is not proof of authorization.
The MCP specification describes clientInfo as self-reported and not verified by the protocol; it is not used as authenticated system/delegate identity.
Self-reported server implementation metadata is not used as authenticated identity or authorization evidence.
Current adapter sidecar supplies the authenticated agent identity because MCP clientInfo is not security identity.
MCP tool execution alone does not establish delegated scope.

mappings.source_expression: external authorization decision associated with request id
mappings.notes: Approval/denial remains separate from protocol success/failure.

mappings.source_expression: external authorization decision timestamp associated with request id
mappings.notes: Required to test whether approval preceded consequential execution.
Arguments are deliberately omitted from the current canonical record.
Result bodies are deliberately omitted from the current canonical record.

profiles.notes: PROV supplies provenance semantics, not a complete authorization policy model.

mappings.notes: Candidate fit for represented human/software/organization actors.
Candidate fit for consequential or otherwise material activity identity.
Candidate fit for source/evidence entities.
Can support an event-to-source provenance edge.
Useful delegation provenance, but not sufficient evidence that a specific operation was authorized for a scope or time window.

profiles.notes: Fine-grained authorization_details can support normalized scope evidence; bearer credentials themselves are excluded.

mappings.notes: Application-specific authorization detail types require an explicit normalization profile.

mappings.source_expression: authorization server decision record tied to authorization_details
mappings.notes: RFC 9396 structures requested/granted authorization details; deployments still need auditable decision evidence for individual actions.

mappings.source_expression: access token / refresh token / client secret
mappings.notes: Bearer credentials and secrets do not belong in the Activity Record or Receipt.

profiles.notes: C2PA content provenance can complement operational provenance for produced/consumed assets. Candidate-record-v0.1 retains only URI/hash support; richer manifest, AI-disclosure, and repository-receipt evidence is evaluated through the standalone external evidence-reference research profile.

mappings.notes: A canonical source can carry an external content-provenance reference without claiming C2PA conformance.
Digest evidence may be referenced when produced by a valid C2PA workflow.

The current canonical record has no dedicated AI disclosure field. Evaluation favors an external content-provenance evidence reference with explicit validation state rather than copying the assertion into candidate-record-v0.1.

C2PA 2.4 repository-ingestion proofs are evaluated as externally referenced evidence. Candidate-record-v0.1 has no dedicated field and the repository-specific proof body is not copied into the Activity Record/Receipt.

profiles.notes: Agent discovery and task/message evidence are useful, but discovery metadata is not automatically authenticated actor identity.

mappings.notes: Candidate workflow/run correlation input; exact normalization remains profile-specific.
Discovery metadata alone is not used as authenticated system or delegate identity.

mappings.source_expression: authenticated transport/application identity associated with the A2A interaction
mappings.notes: Security identity must come from authenticated context, not from discovery metadata alone.
Requires an explicit state-normalization profile before implementation.

profiles.notes: Delegation/impersonation token-exchange semantics can contribute authenticated actor and scope evidence. Historical nested actor claims are provenance, not automatic current authorization. Raw tokens remain excluded.

mappings.source_expression: validated subject identity from subject_token / issued-token top-level subject claims
mappings.notes: Only validated/trusted subject identity evidence should support the principal; the raw subject_token is not copied.

mappings.source_expression: validated current outermost act actor identity
mappings.notes: RFC 8693 act identifies the current actor. A future multi-hop record may preserve the full actor path separately.

mappings.source_expression: validated current outermost act actor identity
mappings.notes: When the current actor is the executing agent, validated actor identity can support system.agent_id.

mappings.source_expression: nested act claims representing prior actors
mappings.notes: candidate-record-v0.1 has no multi-hop delegation-chain field. Prior nested actors are historical provenance rather than independent current access-control authority.

mappings.source_expression: validated issued-token scope claim / authorization result
mappings.notes: Scope evidence must be normalized to the application's operation vocabulary; raw token text is not copied.

mappings.source_expression: validated top-level nbf or equivalent token-validity evidence
mappings.notes: Token-validity time may bound usable delegated authority but does not by itself prove a per-action approval.

mappings.source_expression: validated top-level exp or equivalent token-validity evidence
mappings.notes: Expiration may bound usable delegated authority and should not be inferred from nested historical actor claims.
may_act can support eligibility to become an actor, but candidate-record-v0.1 has no per-hop delegation authorization field and the claim is not proof that a later action occurred or was approved.

mappings.source_expression: access token / subject_token / actor_token raw token material
mappings.notes: Bearer/delegation credentials and raw token material do not belong in the Activity Record or Receipt.
